hints.text: Start with the sign-in logs for one account. Which account is the employee reporting about?
Try: logs search source=auth user=j.smith. Look for failures, then a success from somewhere new.
The story spans the sign-in logs, the MFA log and the member portal. Search user=j.smith across all sources and collect EVT-001 to EVT-005.
A fact is something the evidence shows. Which events happen one after another?
Record one fact that cites the failures and the success together, one for the MFA change and one for the portal access.
Use case note CASE-001 "..." kind=fact evidence=ev_001,ev_002,ev_003 and repeat for the MFA change and portal access, citing their evidence ids.
What can you prove, and what are you only guessing? Keep those in separate entries.
You need at least two facts with evidence, and at least one hypothesis or unknown, for example whether any member data was copied.
Add an unknown such as "Was any member data copied?" with kind=unknown. Avoid stating data was stolen as a fact.
Which systems did the activity touch, and how serious is it?
The employee workstation and the member support portal are involved. Use case scope and case severity.
Try case scope host_014,member_portal and case severity high.
Think about what could go wrong if you act too fast, and if you act too slowly.
Type case recommend to see the options. Which one confirms the facts before changing anything?
Verifying with the employee and checking impact, then protecting the account, balances speed and harm.
Imagine the SOC lead reading this with no time. What do they need to know?
Write a short summary of what happened and your recommendation with case report, then pick who to escalate to with case escalate.
Try case report CASE-001 "..." with at least a sentence or two, and case escalate soc_lead.
